chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Shadhawayh al-Mu'addib (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Ja'far ibn Jami' narrated to us from his father. He said: Ya'qub ibn Yazid narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Aban ibn Uthman from Aban ibn Taghlib from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn the Master of Worshipers, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali the Master of Martyrs, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib the Master of Deputies (peace be upon them). He said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever blesses me without blessing my family will not find the fragrance of Paradise, and indeed its fragrance can be found from the travel distance of five hundred years.

key_terms.آلي: My family (Ali) — the Ahl al-Bayt, the Prophet's household, specifically referring to his immediate family through Fatima and Ali
key_terms.ريح الجنة: The fragrance of Paradise — a metaphor indicating nearness to or awareness of heavenly reward
key_terms.صلى علي: Blessing upon me (salawat) — the act of sending blessings upon the Prophet, prescribed in the Quran (33:56)

ai.seo_question: What happens if you bless the Prophet Muhammad without blessing his family according to Islamic hadith?
ai.summary: Through a golden chain (silsilat al-dhahab) passing through all the Imams from Imam al-Baqir back through Imam Zayn al-Abidin, Imam al-Husayn, and Imam Ali (peace be upon them all), the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declares that sending blessings (salawat) upon him without including his family (Ahl al-Bayt) is an incomplete blessing that bars one from even detecting Paradise's fragrance, despite it being perceptible from a distance of five hundred years. This hadith is foundational to the Shi'a practice of always including the Prophet's family in the salawat formula.
